newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Rao faces ruling on arrest protection plea.
newsitem.headline: India's Rao faces ruling on arrest protection plea.

text.p: An Indian court on Wednesday was set to decide whether former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao could be arrested in a criminal forgery case that has sent tremors through the nation's political system and stock markets.

Delhi High Court Judge S.K. Mahajan was expected to announce his decision on Rao's plea for legal protection against arrest in the seven-year-old case shortly after the session starts. It was scheduled for 2 p.m. (0830 GMT)
The forgery case is one of two criminal cases against Rao, who served as prime minister from mid-1991 until last May when his Congress party was defeated in general elections.

Rao stepped down as party leader last month when a judge upheld a summons ordering him to appear in court in a separate case of criminal conspiracy to cheat a businessman of $100,000 in 1983. Rao has said he is innocent.
The former prime minister's legal troubles have jolted the fragile political balance that resulted from May's inconclusive poll.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's minority government depends on Congress to weather a potential parliamentary challenge by the opposition Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
Before he quit as Congress leader, Rao pledged support to Deve Gowda's centre-left coalition, saying his party wanted above all to prevent the right-wing BJP from taking power.
Congress and Deve Gowda's United Front claim the BJP, which draws its strength from India's Hindu majority, is a divisive force. The BJP says India is united by a single, Hindu culture.

But Congress's new leader, Sitaram Kesri, has threatened to withdraw his party's support for Deve Gowda if the United Front coalition does not back a Congress alliance in Uttar Pradesh, the most populous state and biggest regional political prize.

Vote counting in assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh began on Wednesday. Analysts predict a hung parliament, with the BJP, the United Front and Congress and its low-caste regional ally all falling short of a majority.

The rumblings of discontent between Congress and the United Front have helped trigger a sell-off in stock markets, which fear a period of political uncertainty could slow the pace of economic reform and discourage foreign investment.

Rao's forgery case dates from 1989. Federal police charged the former prime minister and five others with using false documents to defame a rival politician. Rao, who quit as Congress leader last month, has not commented publicly on the case.
Last week Rao won a temporary reprieve from arrest in the case by requesting anticipatory, or pre-emptive, bail, which amounts to legal protection against arrest.

If the High Court rejects the request for legal protection, Rao is expected to appeal to the Supreme Court. If that petition is turned down, he could be arrested, although government authorities could wait until Rao appears at a hearing on the case set for October 14.
If detained, Rao would be put in custody pending trial. Newspapers said a local hospital had prepared a room for Rao, who suffers from diabetes and heart trouble.

On Monday the Supreme Court reserved judgment on a request by police that a hearing into the separate criminal cheating case be shifted from a crowded local courtroom to a more secure location. It was expected to rule later this week.
Rao had been scheduled to appear on Wednesday in a lower court hearing into the cheating case, but he has been exempted from appearing pending the Supreme Court decision.
